metadata.title: segmento_II.py — vanishing weighted sums of completely multiplicative functions, computed
metadata.description:
One file, Python 3 standard library only, exact integers throughout. No Sage, no numpy, nothing to install. A completely multiplicative function ε with values ±1 can make the weighted sum S(m) = ∑n≤m n ε(n) vanish only when m ≡ 0, 3 (mod 4); the underlying note proves that some ε does for every such m. This tool exhibits those zeros, re-checks the certificates of the proof, and computes the zeros that Legendre symbols carry through a digit recursion.

Thirty seconds. python segmento_II.py autotest recomputes from nothing the worked examples of the note — explicit zeros and the counts a(m), a sample of the block certificates, the digit sets Rq and the zeros they propagate, the loops of the recursion at q = 59, 131, 347, the weighted half sum on all 1510 odd characters of odd conductor f ≤ 121, the null cells of Conrey's function at q = 103 — runs the decoys that must fail, exercises every guard, and ends with SELF-TEST: all correct. If it says anything else, the note and the code disagree and the note is the one to distrust. The archived run ships with it.

What it does. One routine per statement, named after it, usable as a library and as a command line:

  • cero(m) — a completely multiplicative ε with S(m) = 0, the sum recomputed n by n, for admissible m up to 106; for m ≡ 1, 2 (mod 4), the parity reason why none exists.
  • certificado(j) — re-verifies, in integer arithmetic, the 104 interval certificates that prove the theorem for 5000 ≤ m < 108 (2128 pairs of primes, bound at most 0.445), or a single block.
  • digitos(q, s) — the digit set Rq of the Legendre symbol mod q, the class number h(−q) by three routes, and the zeros of S below a bound, each by direct summation and by the digit recursion S(qk + r) = s q S(k) + k(Tq + q C(r)) + T(r); with bloque, the loops of the recursion.
  • semisuma(f) — the weighted half sum ∑c≤(f−1)/2 c χ(c) = (f/2) B1,χ (χ(2)−1 − 1) for every odd character mod f, exactly in Z[ζN], with the vanishing criterion χ(2) = 1 on the primitive ones.
  • conrey(q) — the cells on which Conrey's sine series of the Legendre symbol vanishes identically, computed exactly from its piecewise-linear form; they are the digit set Rq.

What it refuses to do. Above m = 106, cero declines and computes nothing: a zero exists there by the theorem, but the tool does not claim a witness it has not produced. The count of vanishing components is given only for prime conductors, where it is proved. conrey works only for primes q ≡ 3 (mod 4), q > 3, and does not test the positivity that the note's proposition assumes. That is the honesty floor of the note, moved into the code.

Where it comes from. The note Zeros of weighted partial sums of completely multiplicative functions: Dirichlet characters, the Euler factor at 2 and Conrey’s sine series (in preparation) carries the proofs. The tool is not a summary of it — it is the part of it that computes.
